answer: Licensed glacier-station residency proves each applicant in person. A newcomer books a three-day stay at a staffed glacier research station, where the warden checks a government ID, issues a registered locator beacon, and logs daily check-ins; only a completed stay counts. Each stay costs $340, so one honest applicant pays $340 while 1,000 fakes would cost $340,000. The timber lodge, the glacier station, and the beacon registry tie every identity to a real bed, a real warden, and a real device.
